svg.title: Workflow: Publish Article
svg.desc: UML sequence diagram. One PostgreSQL transaction writes the new version, its outbox event and two indexing jobs; a relay publishes them to Kafka and wakes the scale-to-zero indexers, and independent consumers update search, RAG and subscribers at their own pace. Messages: 1. publish(id, version); 2. INSERT version snapshot; 3. INSERT outbox event; 4. INSERT search + RAG jobs; 5. INSERT audit row; 6. 200 published; 7. publish index event; 8. POST /drain/{jobId}; 9. content.search.index.v1; 10. idempotent upsert; 11. ack offset (manual); 12. content.rag.index.v1; 13. chunk + embed; 14. replace chunks; 15. content.notification.*.
svg.text: One PostgreSQL transaction writes the new version, its outbox event and two indexing jobs; a relay publishes them to Kafka and wakes the scale-to-zero indexers, and independent
consumers update search, RAG and subscribers at their own pace.
Cloud Run identity token · wakes the consumer
Transactional outbox: the events exist if and only if
the commit does, so there is never a dual write
At-least-once delivery: consumers write idempotently and ack only after the write. If a wake call fails, the job stays leased
and is replayed when the lease expires.
Result: Content searchable, retrievable and queued for subscribers without a dual write
